facility_roles.note: SLD was built and operated at SLAC on the SLC beam line.
The SLC polarized electron and positron beams that SLD recorded were produced and accelerated entirely at SLAC.

intervals.quote: It was moved onto the SLC beam line in November 1990 for final checkout.

intervals.quote: It was moved onto the SLC beam line in November 1990 for final checkout.

intervals.label: first data run (22% polarized beam)
intervals.quote: During 1992, 11,000 Z's were collected in the SLD with a 22% polarized e- beam colliding with an unpolarized e+ beam. A second data run began in February 1993, with polarization greater than 60%.

intervals.label: SLC/SLD physics running
intervals.note: INSPIRE's date_started (1991-04) is slightly earlier than the 1992 first-Z-collection date on the official SLD intro page; both are recorded (see the "final checkout" and "first data run" intervals above) rather than reconciled to one number.

physics_goals.quote: Studies include (1) precision tests of the Standard Model of the electroweak interactions and the Z partial width to bottom states, particularly by measuring the left-right polarization asymmetry A(LR).
physics_goals.value: Precision tests of the Standard Model electroweak interactions, particularly the left-right cross-section asymmetry A_LR at the Z pole, plus heavy-flavor (B and charm) physics and tests of QCD in multi-jet events

summary.plain: A general-purpose particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, that used a uniquely highly polarized electron beam to make some of the most precise measurements of how the Z boson decays. It ran from 1991 to 1998.
summary.technical: General-purpose detector at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC) e⁺e⁻ Z factory; unique among the LEP/SLC-era Z-pole detectors for a highly polarized electron beam (>60% from 1993), used chiefly for a precision measurement of the left-right asymmetry A_LR and sin²θW_eff, plus heavy-flavor and QCD studies. First data 1991-1992, ran to June 1998.

unique_capabilities.quote: For precision studies of electroweak physics with the Z, the SLD is the only e+e- detector to have access to a highly polarized electron beam, thereby allowing certain electroweak measurements at SLC to surpass those being made at LEP, the European e+e- collider, using unpolarized beams.
unique_capabilities.value: The only e⁺e⁻ Z-factory detector with access to a highly polarized electron beam, letting certain electroweak measurements surpass the precision reachable at LEP with unpolarized beams
